session_note: Louisiana's 2026 Regular Session convened Monday, 2026-03-09 and adjourned sine die Monday, 2026-06-01, confirmed directly via legis.la.gov's session information. Both 2026 RS bills in this packet (HB1206, HB922) show, on the legislature's own bill-status pages queried after that date, no action beyond their spring 2026 committee considerations and no committee report (favorable or unfavorable) -- with the session now closed, they are treated as died in committee. The 2024 RS and 2025 RS enactments (Act 730, Act 36) are reconfirmed unchanged, since Louisiana does not un-enact laws. The 2025 RS concurrent resolution (HCR61) was adopted by the House but never taken up for Senate concurrence, so it died when the 2025 RS ended.

decisions.notes: Packet's April 2026 snapshot ('Pending... referred 2026-04-01') is superseded by the 2026-04-28 committee-consideration entry, but the bill never advanced past that point; with the regular session now adjourned sine die, it is dead for the 2026 RS. Confidence is not higher because the official page does not print an explicit 'involuntarily deferred'/'failed in committee' phrase -- it only shows no further action, combined with the confirmed adjournment date, as evidence of death in committee per the task's guidance.

fields.status: Adopted by House 93-0 on 2025-06-08; received by Senate same day but never brought up for concurrence -- returned to Senate calendar subject to call 2025-06-09 and died there when the 2025 RS ended

evidence.title: HCR61 (2025 Regular Session) - Louisiana State Legislature bill information
evidence.supports: Confirms the full action history ends with the Senate reading the resolution by title and returning it to the calendar 'subject to call' on 2025-06-09, after House final adoption 93-0 on 2025-06-08; there is no later entry showing Senate adoption or concurrence, and the page's current status field, queried 2026-07-31, is unchanged from that 2025-06-09 state.
evidence.quote: Current Status: Subject to call - Senate referral

decisions.notes: Packet's status text is still verbatim current on legis.la.gov, confirming no change occurred. As a concurrent resolution it required action by both chambers; the Senate never concurred, so it died without final adoption at the close of the 2025 RS. bill_status_category is set to failed_died (rather than left as an ambiguous 'pending' read) because no subsequent session action exists and Louisiana concurrent resolutions do not carry over between regular sessions.
